# About the United Americas [italic]A union of the Americas, carried out among the stars.[/italic]
## Who We Are The [bold]United Americas[/bold] was founded in 2104, when the nations of North, Central and South America joined their governments, their fleets and their industry into a single union. Eighty years on it fields one of the strongest militaries in human space and the deepest industrial base on the frontier.
## Government - An elected [bold]President[/bold] and [bold]Vice President[/bold] lead the Union from Earth. - A [bold]Congress[/bold] seats representatives of every member nation, and sets the law that follows a citizen to any world. - Most American colonies lie in the [bold]American Arm[/bold] of the Outer Rim. Others, like those of this sector, are strung out along the frontier, a long way from home.
## Serving the Colonies - [bold]Colonial Administration[/bold] exists to protect the lives and rights of American colonists and to keep their settlements running. - The [bold]Colonial Marshal Bureau[/bold] is its law enforcement arm. Where a colony has a Marshal, it has American law. - Federal agencies, among them the FBI, the DEA and the ATF, still work cases that cross colony lines.
## Defending the Colonies The [bold]United Americas Allied Command[/bold] directs the forces of every member nation: - the [bold]United States Colonial Marines[/bold], older than the Union itself; - the [bold]Latin American Colonial Navy[/bold] and its Landing Forces; - the [bold]Canadian Colonial Armed Forces[/bold], the [bold]UA Colonial Guard[/bold], the [bold]Outer Rim Defense Fleet[/bold] and others.
## The Mission Here This embassy speaks for the Union in the [bold]Neroid Sector[/bold], where every great power keeps a foothold and none holds the whole. Since Allied Command drew back its forces from much of the sector, this mission is often the only face of the Union a colonist will see. The Ambassador represents the President to the colony, its administration and the other missions on station. The embassy does not command troops, and it does not comment on the politics of serving officers.
